content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-16|USDT Payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-building-crypto-store-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-workers-crypto-payment-webhooks-what-actually-how-11|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]]-pages-complete-infrastructure-25|building]] on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Stock photos

Stripe's decision not to support Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ethiopia, and dozens of other countries is not a technical limitation — it is a business decision driven by correspondent banking requirements, local regulatory compliance costs, and risk modeling. PayPal operates the same way. The practical result is that a creator in Lagos with a real product, a real audience, and a real income goal is blocked at the infrastructure level before any transaction ever occurs. Understanding this is the first step toward choosing a different architecture. The correct response is not finding a compliant workaround inside the conventional system. It is building on infrastructure that does not require banking partnerships, local regulatory agreements, or platform permission to operate. NOWPayments operates on blockchain rails that bypass every one of these constraints.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

This infrastructure utilizes a combination of free and paid tools, including GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage. Automatic crypto payment processing is facilitated through NOWPayments, enabling creators to receive payments in over 300 cryptocurrencies with a low 0.5% fee and no KYC requirements.
Who This Is Built For and Why

NOWPayments operates as a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 cryptocurrencies including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT on multiple chains, Solana, BNB on Binance Smart Chain, and Tron. When a buyer initiates payment, NOWPayments creates a unique payment address for that specific transaction, monitors the blockchain in real time, and fires a webhook when payment confirms on-chain. The 0.5% fee is the only cost — no monthly fee, no setup fee, no revenue share, no payout schedule. Funds go directly to the wallet addresses you configure. COREMERCH never touches your wallet or your funds at any point before, during, or after deployment.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure empowers digital creators to own their sales process.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The components of sovereign commerce infrastructure work together seamlessly to provide a comprehensive solution. For instance, Cloudflare Pages and Workers offer fast, secure, and reliable hosting and backend logic, while Supabase provides a robust database for storing orders. NOWPayments integrates with this setup to enable automatic crypto payment verification, ensuring that creators can focus on their products rather than payment processing.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure today, creators can start by selecting the right components for their needs. This might involve choosing between GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages for hosting, deciding on a backend logic solution, and setting up order storage with Supabase or Google Sheets. With the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), creators can have a fully operational online store with automatic crypto payment processing and instant product delivery, all set up within 48 hours.

To sell digital products without Stripe or PayPal, creators can leverage sovereign commerce infrastructure, which provides a base-layer solution for owning and operating a digital commerce stack. This approach ensures that creators have full control over their sales process and are not dependent on platforms that may restrict their access due to location.

For creators looking for a straightforward solution, the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) offers a comprehensive package that includes deployment within 48 hours, Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments integration. More information on this and other solutions can be found at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html, providing a clear path to selling digital products without the need for restricted platforms.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure, start by selecting your hosting platform, such as Cloudflare Pages. Next, choose a backend logic solution like Cloudflare Workers. Then, set up order storage with Supabase. After that, integrate NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment processing. Finally, configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for secure email communications, and test your setup end-to-end to ensure everything works smoothly.
